stem: A fintech company runs a mission-critical relational database on EC2 that requires guaranteed IOPS in the hundreds of thousands with sub-millisecond average latency and the highest available EBS durability.

choices.text: A gp3 general purpose SSD volume
An io1 Provisioned IOPS SSD volume
An st1 Throughput Optimized HDD volume

rationale: io2 Block Express is the highest-performance EBS type, delivering up to 256,000 IOPS and 4,000 MiB/s with sub-millisecond average latency and 99.999% durability, matching every part of this requirement. gp3 can be provisioned up to only 80,000 IOPS, well short of the hundreds-of-thousands ceiling this database needs. io1 tops out at 64,000 IOPS and 1,000 MiB/s with lower durability than io2 Block Express, so it falls short of both the IOPS ceiling and the durability bar. st1 is priced by throughput rather than IOPS and is built for large sequential workloads, not a low-latency, high-IOPS database.
